transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... my primary doctor wanted me to come in. She seems concerned that my meal planning has gotten... too tight, I guess. 

Though to me, it just feels like... well, just keeping breakfast to a yogurt, and... maybe skipping lunch if I’m busy. And then just making a very measured dinner. It just helps keep the day orderly, that's all.
Do you find yourself making these strict meal plans because you’re worried about your weight or shape?

I suppose... yes, partly. It's just... if I step on the scale and it's up, even just a pound, after I've eaten a regular dinner or... or gone to a restaurant... I just get this... this sharp panic. Like I've completely lost control of things. And then I just feel like I have to... fix it the next day. So the planning just prevents that.
After eating, do you ever make yourself sick, exercise excessively, or use laxatives or diuretics to prevent weight gain?
No... no, I don't do anything like that. I don't take anything or... make myself sick. I just stick to the plan.
Do you avoid eating certain foods completely or limit yourself to such a degree that you aren't getting enough nutrition, or do you rely on supplements to make up for what you're not eating?
No... I don't take any supplements. And I don't cut out everything, I just... I eat regular food. I just keep the amounts precise. I'm sure I get enough.
Would you say you have a fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even if you were already underweight?
I think I mentioned this already... but yes. If I see the scale go up... even just a pound, I just... I get that sharp panic I talked about. Like I've lost control. So... yes, I suppose I do.
Do you feel that your body shape or weight influences how you see yourself overall, or how you think others see you?

I suppose it does. I mean... I know I'm an older woman, I'm not trying to look young or anything. But... I still judge how well I'm handling myself by how my clothes fit. Just... whether my waist and hips look contained, I guess. That's how I know I'm doing okay.
Between your controlled eating days, do you ever have episodes where you feel like you lose control and eat a large amount of food in a short period of time?
No. I don't do that. I just... stick to my routine.
Have you noticed your weight being significantly low, or have others expressed concern about your weight loss?

I suppose... well, my doctor mentioned it. He said my weight has drifted down more than he'd like. But... I don't know. When I look at the chart, I just think... a little lower would be a cleaner number. More manageable.
Do you believe that your body weight or shape is significantly different from what others would see, or do you feel that you need to be thinner even if others might say you are already thin?

I don't know about what others see. I just... I don't feel like I'm thin enough. It just feels like there's always a little more I could do to be... tighter. More in control. I don't really care what other people think about it.
Do you believe that being thinner would improve your health or help you feel more in control of your life, or is it more about how you see yourself physically?

I don't really think about the health aspect. And I know I’m an older woman... I'm not trying to look young or anything like that. It's just... I suppose I still judge how well I’m handling myself by whether my waist and hips look... contained in my clothes. It just lets me know things are in order. That's all.
Can you tell me what your current weight is, and has your doctor mentioned if it's below a healthy range for someone your height and age?

I weigh 98 pounds. And yes, my doctor has brought it up. She says it's medically unsafe, but... I don't know. I think she's overstating it, honestly. I'm still working full time as an analyst. I run my own errands. I manage my life just fine. So I don't really see how it's as dangerous as she makes it out to be.
Do you see your current weight as a problem, or do you feel that your doctor is wrong in calling it a concern?

I don't see it as a problem, no. Like I said, when she tells me it's medically unsafe, I just... I think she's exaggerating. I go to work every day. I do my shopping. I handle my life. If it were really that bad, I wouldn't be able to do those things.
Do you feel that you are heavier than you actually are, or do you feel that your body looks heavier in certain areas than what others might see?
I don't know about what others see. I just... I look in the mirror, and I see areas that need work. My stomach, mostly. It's just... I can see where it's not right.
Can you tell me your height, so we can determine if your current weight of 98 pounds falls significantly below a healthy range for someone your age and stature?

I'm 5'6". And yes, I know... my weight has drifted down more than my doctor likes. But honestly, when I look at the chart, I just... I still find myself thinking that a little lower would be a cleaner, more manageable number.
